items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: you know. the very famous dance hall here on Sunset Boulevard that had bands coming in all the time, Gene Krupa, Tommy Dorsey, and what other bands were there?

ctx.x: Was Hollywood or Los Angeles somewhat starved for this big band sound that you were providing, because you seemed to really hit a popular wave here of acceptance that you might not have even had in other locations.

There might have been part of that, I’m not sure, because I think big bands were coming in and out, you know. But gee, what other big bands were playing? Yeah, there was the Palladium, you know, the very famous dance hall here on Sunset Boulevard that had bands coming in all the time, Gene Krupa, Tommy Dorsey, and what other bands were there? Others that I can’t even recall, but they were coming. There were theaters, too, you know, theaters going that had stage shows. Oh, and there was also the Casa Mañana, which…

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...after, you know, at the height of the Benny Goodman, Glenn Miller, Harry James, Gene Krupa, you know, everybody was coming out of the bands...

ctx.x: He says in August of 1933 he signed a contract with a financial backer to support a mixed Big Band, which had Alex Hill, as the arranger, to front it. This is in Mezzrow's Mezra's book.

He said "The following agreed to join: Joe Sullivan, Bud Freeman, Floyd O'Brien, Max Kaminsky, Gene Krupa, Eddie Condon and Pee Wee Russell. We rehearsed and the future looked good and we were okay for a sustaining program on a network, but soon after, the men in the band left him to go to a rehearsal arranged by Red McKenzie for some other guy who claimed he was a politician's son ..."
Do you remember any of these details? I mean you may not have been around ...
